notes: OpenCode 2.x through the service API (#2109 P5b-2). A user shell escape (POST /shell, `echo hello`) between two turns. The escape is not a model turn: the session stays ready through it — at least 10s of ready with no working and no waiting after turn 1 — and turn 2 still drives working → ready. Exactly two readies, one per turn.

text: The API session is admitted when its first activity lands (P3, #2107): a ses_… transcript_new. Its first state is not pinned — an API session is first seen working (P4; P5a's smoke cells)
The session binds to the one running 2.x service (pid.go servicePIDFor) — there is no client process
Turn 1 drives the session to working
The 2.x plugin's session.execution.succeeded ends turn 1 (recorded as the canonical Stop hook)
Turn 1 completes; the session then holds ready through the shell escape — no working and no waiting for at least 10s
After the escape a real prompt still drives ready → working
The 2.x plugin's session.execution.succeeded ends turn 2 (recorded as the canonical Stop hook)
